body: Three badges and no list. The listing prints 100% vegan, non-GMO and wildcrafted botanicals, and does not name one plant in the formula.
The serving is two capsules a day with meals. The capsule count and the milligrams in a capsule are not printed.
Two capsules a day, with a meal.

The listing does not say which meal. Two a day is the printed serving. The listing prints no maximum; the statutory line at the foot of this page is where do not exceed the stated dose comes from. Either way, a missed day stays a missed day rather than a double dose tomorrow.
Not printed on the listing. Dry, out of direct sun and lid on is what we would do with any capsule. No fridge.
Not for children. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, or you take prescribed medication, ask your GP or pharmacist before you start.
A vegan badge tells a pharmacist nothing about what is in the capsule. Without the list, nobody can check this jar against a prescription.
Sent out from 599 Smithdown Road, Liverpool, Tuesday to Sunday. UK delivery is free over £50, or you can collect from the shop between 10 and 6, any day except Monday.

No plant is named, no part of a plant is named, and no amount is given, so the frames below stay empty rather than carry a photograph of something we have guessed at.

doctrine.h3: We publish the specification. We do not publish claims about what it does.
doctrine.p: What we have to publish here is three badges and a serving. The sheet says not printed wherever that is the truth, including for the list of plants, and the page carries no sentence about what the formula is for. Badges are easy to print. A list is the hard part, and it is the part that is missing.

spec.intro: Three badges, a serving and a price is the whole of what this listing gives us. The rest of the sheet says so.

reiss.label: From Reiss
paras: Vegan, non-GMO, wildcrafted. I have printed all three on this page because the listing prints them and they are checkable, and I have then had to write the same sentence three times: none of them tells you what is in the jar. A capsule can be vegan and contain nine plants I have not named, and it would still carry every badge.

The reason a list matters is dull and practical. Somebody comes into the shop on four prescriptions and asks whether this one is all right alongside them. With a list I can read it out and they can take it to a pharmacist. Without one, the only honest answer is that nobody can tell, and I would rather say that on the page than at the till after the money has changed hands.

So the sheet above prints what exists and leaves the rest blank. If the label prints a list, it goes on here in full, in Latin, with the part of each plant named, in the order it is declared. That is what the Decolonise sheet looks like and it is what this one should look like.
reiss.pull: A capsule can carry every badge on the shelf and still not tell you what is in it.
